top_choice_rationale: P001 (B001: Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn) is the only substantive proposal on the slate. It rewards a mature measurement advance: estimating demand and competition with endogenous prices in differentiated-product markets, with dynamic-industry models as context. It made counterfactuals on substitution, markups, mergers and welfare answerable that earlier reduced-form work could not. It has about thirty years of use in regulatory practice and has spread into trade, health and environmental economics. Its sensitivities to numerics, instruments and functional form are documented. The central 1995 paper is jointly authored by the three named laureates, so credit fits the three-laureate cap without splitting a result. Reservations remain: toolkit versus discovery, the omission of Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin, and a citation that should not overstate robustness. My view of the evidence rests on background knowledge and round-2 statements, not independent verification. These reservations do not outweigh no award, so P000 is ranked last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no tie to Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn. My field is political science, and I gave the 2024 presentation speech on institutions and prosperity. That speech does not establish a personal preference. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
